# Wilmington University Corner

> A law school study library: outlines, rule charts, flowcharts, flashcards, and practice question banks you can open in the browser or download.

Machine-readable endpoints (static JSON, CORS-friendly via GitHub Pages):
- [Catalog](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/catalog.json): every subject and document with metadata and URLs
- [Search index](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/search-index.json): compact index for keyword search
- [OpenAPI spec](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/openapi.json): describes the endpoints above
- [Full text](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/llms-full.txt): plain text of every document in one file

## Evidence

Federal Rules of Evidence, Classes 1–19 (Fisher, Evidence, 4th ed.): jury secrecy, relevance and 403, the policy exclusions, character evidence and 404(b), impeachment and the rape shield, hearsay and its exceptions, the Confrontation Clause, Bruton, the right to present a defense, and lay and expert opinion. Includes the outline, rule chart, flowcharts, flashcards, and bar-style practice questions.

- [Evidence Outline](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/documents/evidence/evidence-outline.txt): Outline. Condensed exam outline of Classes 1–19 on the Fall 2026 syllabus (Fisher pp. 1–783). Part I covers the Federal Rules, jury secrecy under 606(b), relevance, conditional relevance, and 403. Part II covers the specialized relevance rules, 407–411. Part III covers character evidence: the propensity ban, 404(b), Huddleston, 413–415, the defendant's and victim's character, and habit. Part IV covers impeachment under 607–609 and the rape shield. Part V covers competency, the definition of hearsay, opposing parties' statements, prior statements of witnesses, and the 803, 804, and 807 exceptions. Part VI covers the Confrontation Clause from Crawford through Smith v. Arizona. Part VII covers completeness, Bruton, and Chambers. Part VIII covers lay and expert opinion from the Week 10 reading. Rule and tip boxes throughout, and a card for every principal case with its class.
- [Evidence Rule Chart/outline](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/documents/evidence/evidence-rule-chart.txt): Rule Chart. The master rule chart for Weeks 1–5. Each rule is explained in plain English with a note on what to watch out for. Rows tagged by class come from the Class 1–10 lecture slides, and there are notes on what the midterm covers.
- [Federal Rules of Evidence](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/documents/evidence/federal-rules-of-evidence.txt): Document. The full official text of all 69 Federal Rules of Evidence, as amended to December 1, 2024. Search by word, phrase, or cite (type 803(2) to go straight to the excited-utterance exception, or 404(b)(2) to see that clause marked), filter to the rules the course covers or to any of nine course topics, and follow cross-references between rules. Each rule shows how often the outline and the practice sets cite it. The practice sets use it for their Look up popup: any rule cited in a question or explanation opens its text with the cited subdivision marked.
- [Evidence Flowcharts](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/documents/evidence/evidence-rule-flowcharts.txt): Flowcharts. Interactive decision charts for Weeks 1–5. Zoom and pan around each chart, walk through a rule one step at a time, and search all nine charts. Covers relevance (401–403), the policy rules (407–411), character evidence, 404(b), impeachment, 609 convictions, the 412 rape shield, and 606(b) jury secrecy.
- [FRE Rule Cards](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/documents/evidence/fre-rule-cards.txt): Flashcards. Flashcards for the Federal Rules of Evidence in Weeks 1–5. Pick your topics, flip each card, and rate yourself with a tap or a swipe. Missed cards come back sooner, and your mastery is saved in your browser.
- [Evidence Rules easy Drill](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/documents/evidence/evidence-rules-drill.txt): Practice Questions. Conceptual multiple-choice questions for Weeks 1–5, weighted toward the Federal Rules. The answer order reshuffles every time you load the page, so you can't memorize the letters.
- [Evidence BAR style questions 1](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/documents/evidence/evidence-case-files.txt): Practice Questions. Bar-level application questions for Weeks 1–5. Each question sets two or three rules against each other and turns on a single fact. Every answer choice has its own explanation, and the set includes one-fact variations and a coverage map.
- [Evidence BAR style questions 2](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/documents/evidence/evidence-case-files-ii.txt): Practice Questions. A second, all-new set of bar-style application questions covering Classes 1–10. Every answer choice has its own explanation. Includes one-fact variations and a coverage map of all 157 outline items.
- [Evidence Mock Midterm](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/documents/evidence/evidence-mock-midterm.txt): Practice Questions. A timed practice exam for the night before the midterm: 60 new bar-style questions on Classes 1–10, in four 15-question parts that each cover every topic at the real exam’s 30-minute pace. Answers stay hidden until you submit. Then you get your score by topic, the rules to review, and an explanation for every choice.
- [Evidence Mock Midterm II](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/documents/evidence/evidence-mock-midterm-ii.txt): Practice Questions. A second timed practice exam: 60 more new bar-style questions on Classes 1–10, with no fact patterns repeated from the first. It has the same four 15-question parts, each covering every topic at the real exam’s 30-minute pace, and draws on textbook problems the first exam didn’t use. Answers stay hidden until you submit. Then you get your score by topic, the rules to review, and an explanation for every choice.
- [Hearsay Practice Exam](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/documents/evidence/evidence-hearsay-practice-exam.txt): Practice Questions. 40 bar-style questions, five choices each, covering all of hearsay: the definition and non-truth uses, opposing-party statements, prior statements and impeachment (613, 806), the 803 and 804 exceptions, 807, multiple hearsay, completeness under 106, and the Confrontation Clause through Smith v. Arizona and Samia. Includes the 2023 and 2024 amendments. Tutor mode grades each question as you go; timed mode gives you 80 minutes and grades at the end with a score by topic. Every question has the rule, an analysis, and why each choice is right or wrong.

## Professional Responsibility

Model Rules of Professional Conduct and MPRE prep, Weeks 1–5 (Chs. 1–9, 20, 21): forming the client-lawyer relationship, competence, confidentiality, conflicts, and the duties that follow a representation from start to finish.

- [Professional Responsibility Outline](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/documents/professional-responsibility/pr-outline.txt): Outline. Exam-prep outline for Weeks 1–5 (Chs. 1–9, 20, 21), organized around the life of a representation. Pinpoint cites point to the readings and class slides, and every rule tested in the practice bank is covered.
- [Pro Rep Drill](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/documents/professional-responsibility/mpre-drill-v3.txt): Practice Questions. 355 original MPRE-style application questions on Chs. 1–9, 20, 21 and the class slides. Use study mode for instant feedback or exam mode to be graded at the end. Filter by topic and shuffle the answer order.
- [MPRE 500: Course Subset](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/documents/professional-responsibility/mpre-500-course-subset.txt): Practice Questions. 298 of the 500 questions in Stevenson, 500 MPRE Practice Questions (2019), limited to what Weeks 1–5 cover. Uses the book's answer key, with study and exam modes, topic filters, and answer shuffling.
- [Course Quiz](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/documents/professional-responsibility/pr-course-quiz.txt): Practice Questions. The 54 multiple-choice questions from the class quizzes on Chs. 5, 6, 8, 20, and 21, checked against the course answer keys. Take the quiz for a score or open the answer view, with explanations drawn from Ethical Lawyering, the class slides, and the Model Rules.

## Con Law II

Constitutional Law II: the First Amendment, Chapters 1–6. Covers the Religion Clauses, the speech framework, incitement and national security, true threats and speech integral to crime, and immoral speech, including obscenity, child pornography, and indecency.

- [First Amendment Outline](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/documents/con-law-ii/first-amendment-outline.txt): Outline. Case-by-case outline of Chapters 1–6, from Barnette and Kennedy v. Bremerton through Counterman, Ferber, and Free Speech Coalition v. Paxton. Each case has its rule, facts, holding, and dissent. Includes the Free Exercise, speech, prior restraint, and immoral speech checklists, along with synthesis tables.
- [First Amendment Flowcharts](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/documents/con-law-ii/first-amendment-flowcharts.txt): Flowcharts. Interactive decision charts for Chapters 1–6. A big-picture map shows how the Religion Clauses and the speech doctrines fit together, and eight charts walk through coercion, Free Exercise, the Establishment Clause and funding, the speech framework, incitement and fighting words, prior restraints, true threats and speech integral to crime, and immoral speech. Tap any box for a plain-English explanation, the cases behind it, and what to watch out for.
- [First Amendment Quick Drill](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/documents/con-law-ii/first-amendment-drill.txt): Practice Questions. 264 multiple-choice questions on every case and concept in the outline. They test what each case held, hypotheticals built on its facts, and how the doctrine applies. Filter by chapter or question type, shuffle the answers, and review only the ones you missed.
- [First Amendment BAR style questions 1](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/documents/con-law-ii/first-amendment-case-files.txt): Practice Questions. Bar-style application questions for Weeks 1–6 (Chapters 1–6). Each question sets out new facts, from compelled pledges and school prayer to protest livestreams, chatbot lawsuits, and age-verification laws, and asks you to apply the doctrine. Every answer choice has its own explanation. Includes one-fact variations and a coverage map of all 113 outline items.
- [First Amendment Case Flash Cards](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/documents/con-law-ii/first-amendment-case-flash-cards.txt): Flashcards. 34 flashcards, one for each main case in Chapters 1–6, from Whitney and Barnette through Paxton and Brown. Each card asks what the case held, then gives the rule, the vote, and the key reasoning. Cited cases such as Gobitis, Yoder, Zelman, and Chaplinsky appear on the card for the case that cites them. Flip each card, then mark it Got it or Revisit.
- [First Amendment Concept Flash Cards](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/documents/con-law-ii/first-amendment-concept-flash-cards.txt): Flashcards. 32 flashcards on the core concepts of Chapters 1–6. Covers the Free Exercise and speech checklists, the ways a law fails neutrality, Establishment Clause funding, RFRA, the unprotected categories, overbreadth and vagueness, prior restraints, mens rea, the Miller test, and protecting kids versus adults.
- [First Amendment Mock Exam](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/documents/con-law-ii/first-amendment-mock-exam.txt): Practice Questions. A timed practice exam covering everything in Chapters 1–6: 60 bar-style questions with new facts, in four 15-question parts that each cover every topic at two minutes a question. Answers stay hidden until you submit. Then you get your score by topic, the rules to review, and an explanation for every choice.
- [First Amendment Case Repetition](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/documents/con-law-ii/first-amendment-case-repetition.txt): Practice Questions. 349 quick questions for Chapters 1–6. 236 drill all 34 cases by their full names: name the case from its facts, its rule, or a key line, then recall its holding, its reasoning, and the cases it overruled or set up. 113 more drill the core concepts and elements across 23 topics, from strict scrutiny and the ways a law fails neutrality to the Brandenburg elements, Counterman’s recklessness standard, and the Miller prongs. Every question carries an illustration; when the picture would give the answer away, it stays blurred until you answer. Filter by chapter, question type, or a single case or topic.
- [First Amendment Case Repetition, Volume 2](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/documents/con-law-ii/first-amendment-case-repetition-vol-2.txt): Practice Questions. 239 new questions on the same 34 cases and 23 topics as Volume 1, asked from different angles. Name each case from a new detail, then recall its holding, its reasoning, and the doctrine around it, plus 45 questions on core concepts and elements. 58 application questions put the rules to new fact patterns and explain why every wrong choice is wrong. Every question carries an illustration; when the picture would give the answer away, it stays blurred until you answer. Filter by chapter, question type, or a single case or topic.
- [First Amendment Essay Questions](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/documents/con-law-ii/first-amendment-essay-questions.txt): Practice Questions. 15 bar-style essay questions covering every case and concept in Chapters 1–6, organized by topic. Each essay sets out new facts with several questions, from a compelled state creed and a noise ordinance aimed at a night ceremony to a leaked convoy memo, threatening messages, and an AI companion app. Open the model answer for a full-credit response worked issue by issue, the cases it uses and why, the key concepts explained, and a 10-point scoring guide. Includes a case index and a coverage map of all 113 outline items.

## Sales and Leases

Sales and Leases of Goods under UCC Articles 1 and 2, Weeks 1–8 (Sepinuck, Chapters 1–6). Covers which law governs, formation and the battle of the forms, the statute of frauds, warranties and disclaimers, gap fillers, delivery and risk of loss, remedies, the parol evidence rule, assignment and delegation, repudiation, and excuse.

- [Sales and Leases Outline](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/documents/sales-and-leases/sales-and-leases-outline.txt): Outline. Condensed outline of Weeks 1–8 for the Week 10 assessment. 16 sections cover the UCC and governing law, formation and § 2-207, the statute of frauds and unconscionability, good faith and modification, express and implied warranties, quantity and price, delivery and risk of loss, disclaimers, remedies, the parol evidence rule, assignment, termination, insecurity and repudiation, and excuse, with worked problems. Case boxes mark main, note, and cited-only cases with their casebook pages and class slides.
- [Sales and Leases Weighted Practice Exams](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/documents/sales-and-leases/sales-and-leases-weighted-practice-exams.txt): Practice Questions. Ten practice exams (150 new questions) for the Week 10 assessment, covering all of Weeks 1–8 with each topic's share set by how testable it is. Tier 1 gets 66 questions on the bright-line rules most likely to be tested: risk of loss and identification, implied warranties, express warranties, title and entrustment, and warranty disclaimers. Tier 2 gets 64: tender, inspection, acceptance and payment, course of performance and waiver, modification, quantity and price, the parol evidence rule, assignment and delegation, insecurity and repudiation, excuse, and remedy limits. Tier 3 gets 20: scope, formation and § 2-207, the statute of frauds, good faith and variation by agreement, and termination. Each exam has 15 stand-alone, five-choice questions in Professor Richardson's sample-exam format, mixing short hypos that ask who wins and why with "Which of the following is NOT…" questions. Wrong answers are built from the near-miss rules she tests, and some questions offer "None of the above," which is sometimes the answer. Every choice has its own explanation. Study mode checks each answer as you pick it; Exam mode lets you answer a full exam and then grade it. Filter by exam or topic, shuffle the questions, and retry the ones you missed.
- [Sales and Leases Acronym Exams](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/documents/sales-and-leases/sales-and-leases-acronym-exams.txt): Practice Questions. Four practice exams (60 new questions) on just the acronyms: the shipping and delivery terms and the course shorthand. 40 questions cover §§ 2-319 to 2-324 and how each term moves the risk of loss: F.O.B. place of shipment and destination, F.O.B. vessel and F.A.S., C.I.F. and C. & F., ex-ship, "no arrival, no sale," C.O.D. and payment against documents, and what happens when there is no term or one side is in breach. The other 20 test the outline's shorthand: SOF, PER, NOM, CoP/CoD/UoT, LD, SOL, GFP and BIOCB, HTA and LOC (with PDM), DTW and CORS (Mathis), and UETA signatures. Each exam has 15 stand-alone, five-choice questions in Professor Richardson's sample-exam format, mixing short hypos that ask who bears the loss with "Which of the following is NOT…" questions. Every choice has its own explanation. Study mode checks each answer as you pick it; Exam mode lets you answer a full exam and then grade it. Filter by exam or topic, shuffle the questions, and retry the ones you missed.
- [Sales and Leases Complete Coverage Exams](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/documents/sales-and-leases/sales-and-leases-complete-coverage-exams.txt): Practice Questions. 31 quick-fire practice exams (465 new questions) that together test every rule and concept from Weeks 1–8. A checklist of 446 rules and concepts, built from every slide in the Week 1 through Week 8 decks, the Sepinuck casebook (cases, notes and assigned problems) and the statutory supplement (UCC text and Official Comments), was used to write them, and every item on it is tested at least once. The questions are short: one- or two-line rule questions and mini-hypos, many of them "Which of the following is NOT…" questions that test four or five rules at once. Each exam has 15 stand-alone, five-choice questions in Professor Richardson's sample-exam format and samples the whole course, from which law governs and the battle of the forms through warranties, risk of loss, disclaimers, remedies, the parol evidence rule, assignment, repudiation and excuse. Wrong answers are the near misses: the common-law rule the UCC changed, the wrong number or section, merchant vs. non-merchant, the rule from the next section over. Some questions offer "None of the above" or "All of the above," and sometimes that is the answer. The 23 questions that change the facts of another question ("Same contract, but…") name the question they build on and show its facts, so shuffling or filtering never leaves you without them. Every choice has its own explanation. Study mode checks each answer as you pick it; Exam mode lets you answer a full exam and then grade it. Filter by exam or by any of 24 topic areas, shuffle the questions, and retry the ones you missed.
- [Sales and Leases Bar Questions](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/documents/sales-and-leases/sales-and-leases-bar-questions.txt): Practice Questions. 272 bar-style multiple-choice questions covering every rule, case, and assigned problem in the Weeks 1–8 outline, across 18 topics from which law governs and the battle of the forms through warranties, risk of loss, disclaimers, remedy limits, the parol evidence rule, assignment, repudiation, and excuse. Each question sets out new facts, and every answer choice has its own explanation. Variations change one fact to test whether the result changes. Filter by topic, shuffle the questions or answers, retry the ones you missed, and use the coverage map to find the questions for any outline item.
- [Sales and Leases Practice Exams](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/documents/sales-and-leases/sales-and-leases-practice-exams.txt): Practice Questions. 19 practice exams (285 questions) for the Week 10 assessment, written in the style of Professor Richardson's sample exam: 15 stand-alone, five-choice questions each, mixing rule questions ("Which of the following is NOT…") with short hypos that ask who wins and why, plus "None of the above" and "All of the above" choices that are sometimes the answer. Each exam samples the whole Weeks 1–8 condensed outline, and together they cover all 16 sections: which law governs, formation and § 2-207, the statute of frauds, good faith and modification, express and implied warranties, title, quantity and price, delivery and acceptance, risk of loss, disclaimers, remedies, the parol evidence rule, assignment, termination, insecurity and repudiation, and excuse. Every choice has its own explanation. Study mode checks each answer as you pick it; Exam mode lets you answer a full exam and then grade it. Filter by exam or outline section, shuffle the questions, and retry the ones you missed.
- [Sales and Leases Practice Exams II](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/documents/sales-and-leases/sales-and-leases-practice-exams-ii.txt): Practice Questions. A second set of 14 practice exams (210 new questions) for the Week 10 assessment, in the same style as the first: Professor Richardson's sample-exam format, with 15 stand-alone, five-choice questions per exam that mix short hypos asking who wins and why with rule questions ("Which of the following is NOT…"), plus "None of the above" and "All of the above" choices that are sometimes the answer. Every fact pattern is new. The cases are tested by application, not recall: instead of asking what happened in Daitom, Casazza, Market Street, Roth Steel, Rogath, Razor, Top of Iowa, or the note cases, each question gives new facts that track the case (a pump buyer's purchase order that reserves its remedies, a lumber mill that threatens to stop shipping, a lamp buyer warned by an appraiser, an e-bike warranty sealed in the box, a farm that goes silent in an inverted market) and asks you to apply its rule. Each exam samples the whole Weeks 1–8 condensed outline, and together they cover all 16 sections and the assigned problems. Every choice has its own explanation. Study mode checks each answer as you pick it; Exam mode lets you answer a full exam and then grade it. Filter by exam or outline section, shuffle the questions, and retry the ones you missed.
- [Sales and Leases Statutory Supplement](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/documents/sales-and-leases/sales-and-leases-statutory-supplement.txt): Document. Every UCC section the Weeks 1-8 outline and the practice sets cite (100 sections from Articles 1, 2, and 9), from Selected Commercial Statutes, 2026 edition, with the Official Comments. Section text is summarized in the statute's own key words and each comment is condensed; comments the outline or the practice questions rely on are marked. Search by word, phrase, or cite (type 2-207 to go straight there), filter by any of the 16 outline sections, follow cross-references between sections, and open or close all the comments at once.
- [Sales and Leases Focused Practice Exams](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/documents/sales-and-leases/sales-and-leases-focused-practice-exams.txt): Practice Questions. Four practice exams (60 new questions) on just four topics: assignment and delegation (§ 2-210), liquidated damages (§ 2-718), warranties (§§ 2-312 to 2-318), and limited remedies (§ 2-719). Each exam has 15 stand-alone, five-choice questions in Professor Richardson's sample-exam format and covers all four topics, with warranties weighted most heavily: express and implied warranties, title and infringement, disclaimers, cumulation, and privity. Every fact pattern is new, cases are tested by application rather than recall, and every choice has its own explanation. Study mode checks each answer as you pick it; Exam mode lets you answer a full exam and then grade it. Filter by exam or topic, shuffle the questions, and retry the ones you missed.
- [Sales and Leases Playlist](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/documents/sales-and-leases/sales-and-leases-playlist.txt): Music. Sixteen study songs that cover all 16 sections of the Weeks 1–8 condensed outline, from which law governs and the battle of the forms through warranties, risk of loss, disclaimers, remedies, the parol evidence rule, assignment, repudiation, and excuse. The main cases are sung through: Daitom, Casazza, Market Street, Roth Steel, Rogath, Orange & Rockland, Mathis, Razor, Santa Fe, Top of Iowa, and NIPSCO. It starts with track 1 and plays straight through; pick any track from the list, at 0.5×, 0.75×, normal, 1.25×, or 1.5× speed.

## Agency & Partnership

Business Associations, Weeks 1–8 (Bainbridge, Park & Rodrigues, 6th ed.). Covers creating an agency, actual and apparent authority, ratification and estoppel, a principal's tort liability, agents' fiduciary duties, choosing an entity, partnership formation under the UPA and RUPA, partners' rights, authority and duties, dissociation and dissolution, loss sharing, buyout agreements, limited partnerships, and LLCs.

- [Agency & Partnership Outline](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/documents/agency-and-partnership/agency-and-partnership-outline.txt): Outline. Condensed exam outline of Weeks 1–8, built from the Class 1–8 slides, the casebook, and the 2026 statutory supplement. Part I covers agency: creating the relationship, contract liability and authority, tort liability, and fiduciary duties. Part II covers business entities: choosing an entity, partnership formation, economic rights and property, management and authority, partners' fiduciary duties, dissociation and dissolution, Kovacik loss sharing, buyout agreements, limited partnerships, and LLCs. Rule and tip boxes throughout, and a card for every case (62 main cases plus slide references and supplemental readings).
- [Agency & Partnership Bar Questions](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/documents/agency-and-partnership/agency-and-partnership-bar-questions.txt): Practice Questions. 284 bar-style multiple-choice questions covering every rule, case, and slide problem in the Weeks 1–8 outline, across 23 topics: creating an agency, actual, apparent and inherent authority, ratification, estoppel, agents' contract and tort liability, scope of employment, independent contractors, and agents' fiduciary duties; then entity selection, partnership formation, property, management and authority, partners' duties, dissociation and dissolution under the UPA and RUPA, loss sharing, buyouts, limited partnerships, LLPs, and LLCs. Each question sets out new facts, and every answer choice has its own explanation. Variations change one fact to test whether the result changes. Filter by topic, shuffle the questions or answers, retry the ones you missed, and use the coverage map to find the questions for any outline item.
- [Agency & Partnership Practice Exams](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/documents/agency-and-partnership/agency-and-partnership-practice-exams.txt): Practice Questions. 14 practice exams (210 questions) for the Week 10 exam, written in the format of Professor Richardson's sample exam: 15 five-choice questions each, with six stand-alone questions followed by two shared hypos (Q7–11 and Q12–15), and combination choices such as "B and C", "A, B and C", and "None of the above." Together they cover all 14 sections of the Weeks 1–8 condensed outline, from creating an agency through authority, ratification, estoppel, tort liability, and agents' duties, to partnership formation, property, management, partners' duties, dissociation and dissolution under the UPA and RUPA, Kovacik loss sharing, buyouts, LPs, LLPs, and LLCs. Every choice has its own explanation. Study mode checks each answer as you pick it; Exam mode lets you answer a full exam and then grade it. Filter by exam or outline section, shuffle the questions, and retry the ones you missed.
- [Agency & Partnership Practice Exams II](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/documents/agency-and-partnership/agency-and-partnership-practice-exams-ii.txt): Practice Questions. A second set of 14 practice exams (210 new questions) for the Week 10 exam, in the same format as the first: Professor Richardson's sample-exam style, with 15 five-choice questions per exam, six stand-alone questions followed by two shared hypos (Q7–11 and Q12–15), and combination choices such as "B and C", "A, B and C", and "None of the above." All 28 hypos are new fact patterns, among them a term partnership that loses a partner, an art collector's undisclosed agent, a plumber's detour and frolic, a grocery run by three partners, a hospital buyer's self-dealing, a UPA print shop's liquidation, a manager-managed LLC, a joint venture's taken opportunity, an LLP before and after its filing, and a dentists' buyout agreement. Together they cover all 14 sections of the Weeks 1–8 condensed outline, and every choice has its own explanation. Study mode checks each answer as you pick it; Exam mode lets you answer a full exam and then grade it. Filter by exam or outline section, shuffle the questions, and retry the ones you missed.
- [Agency & Partnership Practice Exams III](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/documents/agency-and-partnership/agency-and-partnership-practice-exams-iii.txt): Practice Questions. A third set of 14 practice exams (210 new questions) for the Week 10 exam, in the same format as the first two: Professor Richardson's sample-exam style, with 15 five-choice questions per exam, six stand-alone questions followed by two shared hypos (Q7–11 and Q12–15), and combination choices such as "B and C", "A, B and C", and "None of the above." All 28 hypos are new fact patterns, among them a vineyard partner's expulsion, a nephew selling his aunt's car, a solar lender that runs its borrower, a nightclub bouncer, a UPA laundromat freeze-out, a fired club manager's lingering authority, a coffee franchisor's espresso machines, an LLC formed after its lease was signed, a town's fireworks contractor, a festival lot's taken lease, a surf shop's winding up, and a lender to a cidery. Together they cover all 14 sections of the Weeks 1–8 condensed outline, and every choice has its own explanation. Study mode checks each answer as you pick it; Exam mode lets you answer a full exam and then grade it. Filter by exam or outline section, shuffle the questions, and retry the ones you missed.
- [Agency & Partnership Concept Exams](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/documents/agency-and-partnership/agency-and-partnership-concept-exams.txt): Practice Questions. 14 concept exams (210 questions) for the Week 10 exam, in the format of Professor Richardson's sample exam (15 five-choice questions each, with combination choices such as "B and C" and "None of the above"), but built around the rules rather than long fact patterns. The questions test the fine distinctions: the UPA (1914) against the RUPA on entity versus aggregate theory, property, liability, dissolution, and buyouts; general partnerships against LLPs, LPs, LLLPs, and LLCs on filing, control, liability, agency, and exit; the Restatement (Second) against the Restatement (Third); and which defaults a partnership or operating agreement can and cannot change. Questions 1–6 stand alone, and Questions 7–11 and 12–15 share a focus note naming the topic and statute, such as UPA dissolution, RUPA Article 7 buyouts, LLP shields, or managing an LLC. Every choice has its own explanation, and the exams cover all 14 sections of the Weeks 1–8 condensed outline. Study mode checks each answer as you pick it; Exam mode lets you answer a full exam and then grade it. Filter by exam or outline section, shuffle the questions, and retry the ones you missed.
- [Agency & Partnership Playlist](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/documents/agency-and-partnership/agency-and-partnership-playlist.txt): Music. Study songs that walk through the Weeks 1–8 outline, one topic per track, numbered to match the planned 17-track album. So far: dissociation versus dissolution, winding up and buyouts, Kovacik loss sharing and buyout agreements, and limited partnerships, LLCs, and veil piercing. Pick any track from the list, or let it play through, at 0.5×, 0.75×, normal, 1.25×, or 1.5× speed.

## Contracts I

Contracts I, Weeks 1–9 (Epstein, Markell & Ponoroff, Making and Doing Deals, 7th ed.). Covers whether there is an enforceable agreement, the objective theory of assent, offers and their termination, options and firm offers, methods of acceptance and silence, the mirror-image rule and UCC § 2-207, misunderstanding, indefiniteness and letters of intent, consideration, modification, promissory estoppel, the statute of frauds, duress, and misrepresentation.

- [Contracts I Outline](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/documents/contracts-i/contracts-i-outline.txt): Outline. Condensed exam outline of Weeks 1–9 on the Fall 2026 syllabus. Part I covers formation: enforceable agreements and which law governs, objective assent and implied-in-fact contracts, offers, termination of the power of acceptance, irrevocable offers, acceptance and silence, the mirror-image rule and the battle of the forms, misunderstanding, and indefiniteness. Part II covers consideration, modification, and promissory estoppel. Part III covers the statute of frauds, duress, and misrepresentation. Rule and tip boxes throughout, and a card for every assigned case plus slide references.
- [Contracts I Bar Questions](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/documents/contracts-i/contracts-i-bar-questions.txt): Practice Questions. 266 bar-style multiple-choice questions covering every rule, case, and tip in the Weeks 1–9 outline, across 16 topics from enforceable agreements and the objective theory through offers, termination, irrevocable offers, acceptance and silence, the battle of the forms, misunderstanding, indefiniteness, consideration, modification, promissory estoppel, the Statute of Frauds, duress, and misrepresentation, plus a set of integrated multi-issue problems. Each question sets out new facts, and every answer choice has its own explanation. Variations change one fact to test whether the result changes. Filter by topic, shuffle the questions or answers, retry the ones you missed, and use the coverage map to find the questions for any outline item.

## Civil Procedure

Civil Procedure, Weeks 1–9 (Spencer, Civil Procedure: A Contemporary Approach, 7th ed., and the Federal Civil Rules Supplement). Covers the court systems and sources of procedural law, personal jurisdiction from Pennoyer through Ford, notice and service of process under Rule 4, federal question, diversity, supplemental and removal jurisdiction, venue, transfer and forum non conveniens, the Erie doctrine through Shady Grove, pleading standards from Conley to Iqbal, Rule 11, and responding to the complaint under Rules 8, 12, and 55.

- [Civil Procedure Outline](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/documents/civil-procedure/civil-procedure-outline.txt): Outline. Condensed exam outline of Weeks 1–9 (Classes 1–16) on the Fall 2026 syllabus. Part I covers the civil justice system and the life of a lawsuit. Part II covers personal jurisdiction: the framework, the territorial era, minimum contacts, specific jurisdiction and the stream of commerce, and general, consent, and transient jurisdiction. Part III covers notice and service. Part IV covers subject-matter jurisdiction: federal question, diversity and alienage, supplemental jurisdiction, and removal. Part V covers venue, transfer, forum-selection clauses, and forum non conveniens. Part VI covers the Erie doctrine. Part VII covers pleading, Rule 11, and responding to the complaint. Rule and tip boxes throughout, and a card for every assigned case (29 main cases) plus slide references and supplemental readings.
- [Civil Procedure Bar Questions](https://supertoadman.github.io/Wilmington-University-corner/api/documents/civil-procedure/civil-procedure-bar-questions.txt): Practice Questions. 255 bar-style multiple-choice questions covering every rule, case, and tip in the Weeks 1–9 outline (Classes 1–16), across 15 topics: the court systems and sources of procedural law, the personal jurisdiction framework and territorial era, minimum contacts, specific jurisdiction and the stream of commerce, general, consent, and tag jurisdiction, notice and service under Rule 4, federal question, diversity and alienage, supplemental jurisdiction, removal, venue, transfer and forum non conveniens, Swift to Erie, the modern Erie analysis, pleading and Rule 11, and responding to the complaint, plus a set of integrated multi-issue problems. Each question is an MBE-style fact pattern that asks what a court should do. The four choices are written to the same length and form, and the wrong ones are the usual bar traps: the right result for the wrong reason, a correct rule that does not apply, and a misstated rule. Every answer choice has its own explanation. Variations change one fact to test whether the result changes. Filter by topic, shuffle the questions or answers, retry the ones you missed, and use the coverage map to find the questions for any outline item.
